To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TP53 alterations are frequent in breast carcinoma and associated with poor clinical outcome.
(i) TP53 alterations are found in 26% of primary breast carcinomas, (ii) TP53 alterations were strongly associated with poor prognosis, independent of other known prognostic parameters.
TP53 mutations and nuclear accumulation of p-53 protein are frequent events in primary and metastatic breast carcinoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a group of high-risk patients who could benefit from adjuvant chemotherapy.
the prognostic significance of the p53 tumour suppressor gene.
the prognostic value of TP53 alterations, which is a significant prognostic marker in breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of a TP53 alteration is associated with a poorer prognosis in breast carcinoma.
TP53 alterations in the primary tumour are associated with poor outcome, and this is independent of the presence of other known prognostic factors in the tumour.
TP53 mutations and/or accumulation of p53 proteins are common events in breast cancer and may have a prognostic significance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TP53 mutation and/or nuclear protein overexpression in breast carcinoma is an adverse prognostic marker.
TP53 alterations are associated with poor prognosis.
TP53 mutations and/or accumulation of nuclear p53 protein in primary breast tumour is associated with poor prognosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TP53 mutations and p53 protein accumulation are associated with a more aggressive phenotype and poor clinical outcome in breast cancer.
the presence of TP53 mutations in breast cancer is an independent prognostic indicator for poor outcome.
the TP53 gene has a major prognostic significance for patients with breast cancer, and that the TP53 status should be considered in the clinical management of these patients.
